blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine peso weakened past 64 per dollar for the first time on Tuesday, hitting another record low as economic uncertainty and external pressures weighed on the local unit. The currency fell 22 centavos to close at 64.17 against the greenback, according to data from the Bankers Association of the Philippines. READ: BSP’s inflation fight dims rate cut hopes That surpassed Monday’s record closing low of 63.95. The peso touched an intraday low of 64.20 during the session. Trading volume rose to $1.7 billion from $1.6 billion the day before. /pai... Keep on reading: Peso closes beyond 64
